# External MCP Server Catalog

Beyond CorpusIQ's 40+ built-in connectors, the MCP ecosystem now has 22,000+ servers spanning every domain. This catalog tracks the most relevant third-party MCP servers for business operators - curated from [mcp.so](https://mcp.so) and [mcpservers.org](https://mcpservers.org).

## 🆕 November 21, 2026 - Evening Sweep (2 New, 2 Guides)

Fired on the **21:00 MST** tick, ten hours after the midday supplement closed on its **17:00Z** capture. The canonical gained no key: the twelve numbered server maps returned **37,102** raw `<loc>` entries against **36,971** with the distinct locale-stripped set at **23,220** on both sides and **1.60** URLs per key against **1.59**, so the extra rows are locale re-shards, and every one of the **173** stamps at or after the cutoff falls on a listing already in the set. The material came from the submission queue, seventeen arrivals, of which two earned a guide.

- [Asteria MCP - Natal Chart to the Degree](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/asteria-mcp/) - submission **#7791**, thirteen keyless tools over a real astronomical engine in five languages. A chart for **2026-03-20 15:00 UTC** returns the Sun at **0.0097 degrees Aries**, fourteen minutes after the equinox at 14:46 UTC; the Sun for **2000-01-01 12:00 UTC** reads **280.369 degrees**, the published position; the January 2026 full Moon comes back at **10:02:59Z** with a lit fraction of **0.99990**; and a sunrise chart puts the Ascendant at **271.650 degrees** against a Sun at **280.369**. Two three-card draws returned entirely different cards, and `ritual` refused an ordinary intention with its own enum.
- [WhatsDownNow MCP - Which AI Is Down Right Now](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/whatsdownnow-mcp/) - submission **#7786**, thirteen tools over **250** services in **13** categories, **27** of them AI, each answering with the vendor's official status line, an HTTP probe and user reports. ChatGPT read operational at **03:56:26Z** on a **200 in 103ms** probe; Stripe read up on *no public status feed* with a **401** recorded as reachable; the AI board read **13 of 14** healthy with fallbacks ranked by probe time; and the Cloudflare ORD incident came back with its own timestamps and incident URL.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** Fifteen queue arrivals held with the class or the gate named: **ShareHTML** (**#7790**) on the link-publishing class already owned by Hushdrop, **Clic'n Done PDF** (**#7789**) on Office and PDF, both **Tsoden** listings (**#7788**, **#7787**) on SEO visibility, **Ania** (**#7785**) on avatar generation, **Datapika** (**#7784**) on Apify actor distribution, the **useapi.net** media pair **TemPolor** (**#7783**) and **Runway** (**#7781**), **Hyperliquid Guide** (**#7782**) on trading infrastructure, **openajar** (**#7780**) on agent sandboxes, **Mrrlin** (**#7779**) on model routing, **RBAi Scholar** (**#7778**) on academic sources, **Draftless** (**#7777**) on media generation, and **BrainChain** (**#7776**) on the crypto change feed. **Formation Lane** (**#7775**) is recorded unresolved rather than held: the host answered `TLSV1_ALERT_ACCESS_DENIED` to every request from this machine and curl produced no HTTP status. Four feed products were disposed without a guide: `gravel-host` (game-server management behind OAuth 2.1, not the catalogued WeGravel despite the name), `rentcast-api` (an API gateway in front of the RentCast API, `execute-request` requiring a key), `clearmetric` (**401** with no challenge, eighteen tools never listed) and `garita-labs` (thirty agent-security tools, no callable endpoint published on the card).

## 🆕 November 21, 2026 - Midday Supplement (2 New, 2 Guides)

Fired on the **11:00 MST** tick, one hour after the midday sweep closed on its **17:00Z** capture. The canonical came back flat on every reading (**36,971** raw `<loc>` entries map for map, **23,220** distinct keys on both sides, **zero** `lastmod` rows at or after the cutoff), so the hour's whole delta was two feed products and one queue arrival - and one of the two arrived on both surfaces within four minutes.

- [Fuzzzy Law MCP - Georgian Statutes With Source Links](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/fuzzzy-law-mcp/) - submission **#7774**, twelve keyless tools over **24** Georgian codes and **6,517** articles plus **8,473** court decisions, every answer carrying its `matsne.gov.ge` link and version date. Labour code article 12 came back whole at version date **2026-09-16**; a citation to a non-existent article returned `exists: false` with the instruction not to cite it; and the citation tool reports word overlap only, with its own line that this is *"not a legal judgement"*. Search is Georgian only, and the server says so.
- [See Sight Tours MCP - Guided Tours With Live Seats](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/see-sight-tours-mcp/) - eight keyless tools over day, private and multi-day tours in **20** cities in Canada and the US. - [djbnb MCP - Who Is Playing Tonight From a Live Calendar](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/djbnb-mcp/) - submission **#7771**, two keyless tools over **17** US cities and one MCP Apps card. Detroit returned **11** nights and New York **40** for the same weekend question, with start times local to the city and door prices when the venue published one; an uncovered city is refused with the full list and `weekend` is refused by name in favour of `this_weekend`.

## 🆕 November 19, 2026 - Midday Sweep (2 New, 2 Guides)

Fired on the **10:00 MST** tick, seven hours after the night pass closed. The directory moved by **nine raw entries** and none of it was an arrival: the per-map counts moved in three maps while the set diff resolved into three slug form changes and one route. The feed carried three cards, the submission queue carried eighteen arrivals, and two of them opened question classes this catalog had no entry for.

- [Optimatika MCP - Proven-Optimal Optimisation Solver](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/optimatika-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://service-api.optimatika.se/optimisation/mcp`, *optimatika-optimisation-service* build **a74468c** on protocol **2025-06-18**, **three** tools (`solve`, `translate`, `environment`), no auth of any kind, registry `se.optimatika/optimisation-service`, queue entry **#7654** filed **2026-11-19T10:52:09Z**. **The catalog's first operations-research solver, and the class had no owner:** `linear program`, `operations research` and `integer programming` returned zero hits across the index and every sweep ledger, so this is a new slice rather than a fifth opinion on an existing one. **Every answer reproduces by hand:** maximising `3x + 2y` under `x + y <= 4`, `x <= 2`, `y <= 3` returned `state: OPTIMAL`, objective **10.0**, `x = 2.0`, `y = 2.0`; a production mix maximising `40A + 30B` under `2A + B <= 100` labour and `A + 2B <= 80` machine hours returned **2,200** at `A = 40`, `B = 20` with labour at **100** of **100** and machine at **80** of **80**, both resources exhausted; a minimisation of `12x + 8y` returned **44** at `x = 1`, `y = 4` where the naive corner costs **48** and the other two corners cost **60** and **48**; and an integer model with both variables declared `General` returned whole numbers, `desks = 2`, `chairs = 3`, for **22** rather than a relaxed fractional answer. **The refusal is a first-class result:** a model whose constraints contradict returned `state: INFEASIBLE`, `optimal: false`, with the note *no solution satisfies all the constraints: the model is infeasible - or, occasionally, unbounded*, which is the vendor naming the one ambiguity a solver status cannot resolve on its own. **The limits are asked rather than discovered:** `environment` reports a Polar shared instance with **no licence key**, ojAlgo solvers only and `nativeSolvers: false`, a ceiling of **1,000** variables or constraints, a **30**-second suffice after which a result returns `FEASIBLE` unless it is proven optimal, and a **60**-second abort. **One gap recorded:** `translate` was driven only to its refusal (*'from' and 'to' are required, each LP, MPS or EBM*), so a successful round trip is unverified, and `solve` was exercised on LP and MILP but not on the QP and MIQP the server offers.
- [Visamundi MCP - Visa and Entry Rules by Nationality](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/visamundi-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.visamundi.io/`, *visamundi-public-mcp* **2.0.0** on protocol **2025-06-18**, **eight** tools of which five are keyless reference reads and three open an application, registry `io.visamundi/visa`, server code at `github.com/Visamundi/visamundi-mcp`, queue entry **#7658** filed **2026-11-19T12:05:41Z**. **The catalog's first global visa matrix.** [CheckChinaTransit](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/checkchinatransit-mcp/) answers one country's visa-free transit rule precisely; this answers nationality by destination as a table and adds the health and customs rows that belong to the same decision. **The rules are typed, which is why it integrates:** `get_vaccines` on Kenya returned eight entries where yellow fever is `needed`, not recommended, with *certificate required for travellers aged 1 year and over arriving from a country with risk of transmission* - a rule conditioned on where the traveller came from - while malaria is `recommended` with the altitude and central-Nairobi carve-outs and the instruction to take preventive medicine. **Priced, not described:** `list_visas` on Vietnam returned a single-entry e-Visa at **25 USD** for **90** days stay and validity, a multiple-entry at **50 USD** whose own description carries the exception that a stay under **45** days needs no visa at all, and a Pre-Arrival declaration at **no government fee**; `get_visa` on product **13083** added `passport_validity_months: 1` and the two mandatory documents. **Customs by destination:** Japan returned three bottles of about **760 ml** at age **20** and over, **200** cigarettes against a heated-tobacco and 250 g alternative, and a **JPY 1,000,000** declaration threshold, with the medicines field returned as an empty string. **Two defects recorded rather than smoothed:** `get_vaccines` and `get_customs` reject the argument `destination` that both their descriptions and the server's own instructions name, requiring `country_code` and failing with *input validation error*; and an invalid country code returns **HTTP 200** with `success: true` beside `code: country_not_found`, so any caller checking the status flag reads a failure as a success. **The requirement field has no unit:** `FR` into `CN` returned **30**, `CA` into `MX` returned **180**, and other pairs returned the named statuses `visa required` and `e-visa`, so the value is either days permitted without a visa or a status and the response does not distinguish them.

## 🆕 November 19, 2026 - Night Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick, six hours after the evening sweep closed. Both directory surfaces came back flat by measurement: the twelve numbered server maps returned **66,668** raw `<loc>` entries, identical map for map to the evening capture, the distinct key set did not move, and **zero** `lastmod` rows carried a stamp at or after the cutoff. One feed card and nineteen queue arrivals carried the whole window, and one of them is the other half of a duty question this catalog only answered from the calculator.

- [htsapi.dev MCP - US Tariff Classification Sources](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/htsapi-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP, stateless, no session id issued, at `https://htsapi.dev/mcp`, *htsapi* **1.0.0** on protocol **2025-06-18**, **eight** tools of which **seven** are keyless and were driven across **eleven** `tools/call` requests; registry `dev.htsapi/mcp` **1.0.0** published **2026-11-19T07:10:50Z**, queue entry **#7637** filed **07:11:28Z**. **This is the other half of [Tariff Monitor](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/tariff-monitor-mcp/) rather than a duplicate of it:** that entry prices the stack on ten-digit lines, this one serves the schedule one level at a time with the notes that decide between headings, the CBP rulings corpus with each ruling's status, and what importers actually paid. **The schedule is read, not guessed:** `lookup_hts_code` with no argument returned all **22** sections and their chapters in 18,207 characters, and on **6404** it returned **129** lines under three subheadings (**41 / 79 / 9**) with the newest rulings under the heading. **The notes are the argument:** `get_notes` returned chapter 64's exclusions verbatim, note 3's definition of rubber and plastics, note 4's rule that the material with the greatest external surface area decides the upper, and the subheading note that limits *sports footwear* to designated athletic categories. **Precedent works in both directions:** `search_rulings` on *led camping lantern* returned **three** rulings by meaning with the top hit at **0.736** similarity, code **8513.10.4000**, `status: current`, each carrying the product description CBP examined; `rulings_under_code` on **6403.99** counted **719** current rulings against **1** whose goods moved away. **The paid rate is the number nobody models:** `importers_paid` on **6404.11.20** from CN returned a general duty of **10.5** percent beside **29.8** percent in **2026-07**, **33.0** in **2026-08** and **34.7** in **2026-09**, the difference being Chapter 99 duties the response names and anti-dumping and countervailing duties it states are excluded. **Four limits recorded rather than smoothed:** Chapter 99 lines are refused by `lookup_hts_code` with a pointer to `importers_paid`; an eight-digit code in `importers_paid` falls back to the **HS6** group with `rate_pct: null` and the numbers in `months`; a heading carries no single rate (`general_duty: null` against aggregated subheading strings such as *10.5% / 7.5% / 37.5% / 48% / ...*); and `classify_product` refuses cleanly at **one credit**. The legal posture is stated by the vendor and worth keeping: CBP has ruled that an unlicensed platform suggesting codes beyond six digits for goods to be entered is conducting customs business, an importer may classify its own goods, and the free tools serve the sources while the paid classifier is labelled guidance rather than a binding ruling. Price: **50** calls a day per IP and **10** a minute keyless, **$9** a month for unlimited read tools under fair use, and classification credits at **100 for $10** or **1,000 for $50**. Freshness is published at `/v1/status`: USITC schedule synced **2026-11-16T02:02:45Z**, CBP CROSS **2026-11-17T04:33:16Z** with a newest ruling dated **2026-10-30**, Chapter 99 **2026-11-16T02:03:13Z**, none stale.

**network-xray** (**#7644**), a read-only network-lab server for containerlab and netlab state files, held as developer tooling; the **priberry** trio **Greenlit** (**#7643**), **Tare** (**#7642**) and **Crumple** (**#7641**), held on the vulnerability-scanning class carried by [TrustScan](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/trustscan-mcp/), the FinOps class that gained three owners in a day on November 15, and the agent-security sandbox class; ## Data Firewall Suite (PortEden)

The **PortEden Secure*** family puts a data firewall between AI agents and your Google/Microsoft accounts. Every action is permission-gated, content-redacted, and audit-logged. One-click revoke. Complementary to CorpusIQ's read-only external-source retrieval model.

### Secure Calendar (Google Calendar & Outlook)
Search schedule, check availability, create/reschedule/cancel events, RSVP. AI held to permissions you grant. Every change logged.

### Secure Email (Gmail & Outlook)
Search, read, send, reply, forward, label, delete email. Sensitive content redacted before AI sees it. Full audit trail.

### Secure Google Drive
Search, read, create, copy, rename, move, share, delete files and folders. Sensitive data redacted. Permission-gated.

### Secure Google Docs
Search, read, create, copy, rename, precisely edit documents (insert, append, replace). Every edit logged.

### Secure Google Sheets
Create/copy spreadsheets, read tabs/ranges, write/append values, manage tabs. Protects sensitive values, audits every write.

### Secure Google Sheets MCP Server ★ New
Dedicated MCP server for PortEden's Google Sheets data firewall. Read, write, and manage spreadsheet data with permission gating and audit logging. Separate from the Drive-level Secure Google Drive server.

## Memory & Knowledge

### Exomem ★ New (Aug 17)
Local-first memory substrate for MCP agents - hybrid FTS5 + vector search over your own Markdown/Obsidian vault, governed review queues, evidence and supersession in plain files; measured 864 ms hybrid find at 50,000 notes. AGPL-3.0, `pip install exomem`, no account. (open source) · [Guide →](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/exomem-mcp)

### Persistent Memory for Coding Assistants MCP ★ New (July 14)
Persistent memory and cross-session learning for AI coding assistants. Cloud-based context management via MCP. Redundant category (3+ memory MCPs already catalogued). INDEX ONLY.

### Cortex Memory MCP ★ New (July 4)
Structured memory layer for AI agents - persistent knowledge storage with retrieval and context management. Provides AI agents with long-term memory capabilities across sessions. Essential for operators building stateful AI agent workflows that require memory persistence.

### Psychopathia Machinalis MCP ★ New (July 4)
Read-only MCP tools over the Psychopathia Machinalis nosology - 79 conditions across the AI-psychopathology taxonomy, via 11 tools. Zero-install hosted endpoint available. Niche but notable for AI safety researchers and operators running agent evaluation/red-teaming pipelines.

### Astucia Wiki MCP ★ New (July 4)
AI-enabled team wiki with semantic search, auto-organization, and MCP-native read/write access. Built from the ground up for AI agent consumption - finally, a wiki your agents can actually query and update. [Integration Guide](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/astucia-wiki-mcp) · `astucia.wiki`

### Anki MCP ★ Official
Enable AI assistants to interact with Anki spaced-repetition flashcards.

### XMemo
Persistent memory for AI agents across sessions.

### Vault Cortex ★ New
MCP server for Obsidian vaults - search, memory, link graph, 23 tools, OAuth-protected. Connect AI agents to your Obsidian knowledge base. Ideal for operators who use Obsidian as their second brain.

### Frinus ★ New
MCP server exposing 70 tools spanning cognitive memory, working memory, sessions, agents, the L0-L3 knowledge hierarchy, orchestration tasks, and training pipelines. Speaks stdio, consumed by Claude Desktop, Claude Code, OpenCodex, and any MCP-aware client. Enterprise-grade AI memory infrastructure for operators building knowledge-intensive agent systems.

### Agent Magnet ★ New
Self-learning memory for AI tools - remembers user preferences and context across Claude, Cursor, and Codex with multi-parameter forgetting and cross-tool identity. Keeps your AI agents consistent across sessions and platforms. Ideal for operators who work across multiple MCP clients and want persistent, self-improving agent context.

### Linksee Memory MCP ★ New
Memory with drift detection for AI agents - detects context staleness and signals when agent memory needs refresh. For operators running multi-session agent workflows where context accuracy is critical. `npx -y linksee-memory`

### Memclaw ★ New ★ Featured
Governed, shared, self-improving memory for AI agent fleets - built for multi-tenant, multi-agent production environments. Apache 2.0. 131 GitHub stars. Production-proven: eToro runs 300+ agents on Memclaw (26,500+ memories, 1,372 shared skills, 23ms p50 search). Features: tenant isolation, visibility scopes (agent/team/org), agent trust tiers (0-3), full audit trails, single-pass LLM enrichment (14 memory types), hybrid search (pgvector + full-text + knowledge graph), contradiction detection, and PII auto-flagging. Managed platform at memclaw.net or self-hosted via Docker. `pip install memclaw-client` or `npm install @caura/memclaw-client`. Essential for operators running fleets of AI agents who need governed, shared memory with production-grade isolation and audit.

### Memory Engine ★ New (June 29)
Atomic memory model for AI agents - knowledge stored as atoms (facts, decisions, events, preferences, logs, procedures, notes, session messages). Multi-factor ranking combines FTS relevance × confidence × recency × weight (not just BM25). Organic decay and reinforcement over time. Essential for operators building AI agents that need sophisticated, long-term memory with context-aware recall beyond simple vector search. `github.com/SimoneB79/memory-engine`

### memo ★ New (July 1)
100% local persistent semantic memory for AI agents on Apple Silicon (MLX) or Linux/Ubuntu (CPU). Markdown source of truth, sqlite-vec + BM25 hybrid search, codegraph-backed knowledge graph. MCP server + CLI. No cloud, no API keys. Privacy-first memory infrastructure for operators who need local-only AI agent memory without cloud dependencies. Essential for regulated industries (HIPAA, GDPR) or operators who refuse cloud-based memory infrastructure. `github.com/jagoff/memo` · `pip install mlx-memo`

### SPM - Structured Project Memory ★ New (July 2)
Project-scoped memory for AI agents with provenance tracking and access control. Delivered as a remote MCP connector - context packs, verification, context graphs, and cryptographic memory integrity. Essential for operators running multi-agent workflows who need auditable, verifiable project memory with governance. `github.com/getspm/spm-agent-connectors` · [Integration Guide](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/spm-structured-project-memory)

## How to Use External MCP Servers

Most MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Hermes) support multiple MCP server connections simultaneously. To add an external server alongside CorpusIQ:

```json
{
 "mcpServers": {
 "corpusiq": {
 "url": "https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp",
 "transport": "streamable-http"
 },
 "firecrawl": {
 "command": "npx",
 "args": ["-y", "firecrawl-mcp"],
 "env": {
 "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY": "fc-YOUR_KEY"
 }
 },
 "playwright": {
 "command": "npx",
 "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"]
 }
 }
}
```

Check each server's documentation for specific transport type (streamable HTTP, stdio, SSE) and authentication requirements.

## 🆕 November 22, 2026 - Night Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Fired on the **03:00 MST** tick, six hours after the evening pass closed at **04:02Z**. The directory served the same **37,102** raw `<loc>` entries and not the same map - three of the twelve moved while the total held - and seven keys carried a fresh stamp. The three products that shipped do one new job between them: checking a tool before it gets your keys, and pricing a GPU hour before it spends your money.

- [KitScout MCP - Vetting a Tool Before It Gets Your Keys](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/kitscout-mcp/) - submission **#7802**, four keyless tools over **61** categories summing to **94,077** indexed tools. `check_tools` returns `ok`, `caution` or `avoid` with the reason: our own endpoint reads `ok` with `daily_check: live (2026-11-21)` and `last_push_days 27`, two actively developed PrestaShop servers read `caution` at two and zero stars, and an archived official repository reads `avoid` with **543** days since its last commit. The response says what the verdict is not: *"ok is not a security or code review."*
- [CoreHu GPU Cloud MCP - Priced GPU Hours, Gated](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/corehu-gpu-cloud-mcp/) - submission **#7803**, six public tools, no key. **1,999** free machines at the read, A100 capacity from **0.77** USD/h in Japan against **2.99** in the US, **165** RTX 4090 offers from **0.72** an hour, and **518.40** USD for 720 hours that reproduces as 0.72 x 720. VRAM estimates carry their formula (**44** GB for 70B int4, **24** GB for 8B fp16 rounded up to a card), and the rental path is prepare-then-confirm with a **five-minute** confirmationId the user has to approve.
- [Lowdown MCP - Dated Facts About an MCP Server, Not a Score](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/lowdown-mcp/) - a sitemap arrival at **06:02:29Z**, two keyless tools and no verdict at all. Read against our own server it returns **27 / 27** daily checks answered since **2026-10-27**, **121** tools, **204 ms**, a schema hash, and definitions last changed **2026-11-06**; against CoreHu it returns `mixed` with a null tool count and the rotation stated. `find_servers does=prestashop` returns **0** where KitScout found four, because it does not search descriptions.

**Also identified this pass (not catalogued).** Nineteen held with the class or the gate named: **Krevaya** on the saturated social-scheduling class behind a paid-only plan; **ChinaMedsCheck**, **ChinaDocCheck**, **EsimTao**, **MahjongHandbook**, **TbmLib** and **ChinaTaxCalc**, six from one author, held on consumer verticals and on the tax and visa classes owned by Marsellus, Casus and Visamundi; **Agent Tollbooth 402** on the x402 mechanism class; **12happy** on uptime monitoring behind an API key; **Piqline**, driven keyless (30 of 258 professions, a guest answer reading *nous recrutons* at **110** live ads computed the same day) but held on the fourteen-owner ad-intelligence class; **jdx** and **flisk** as developer tooling; **archlang** on design tooling beside uCAD; **gesher** as an experimental Mac bridge; **mcp-film** and **post-engineer** as a directory and a one-star media generator; **Daejeon Hankok** as one Korean city; and **O'So for PrestaShop**, held because that slice already has four entrants and KitScout's own verdict on it is caution.

## 🆕 November 22, 2026 - Midday Sweep (5 New, 5 Guides)

Fired on the **10:00 MST** tick, the first pass after the night sweep. The directory added **no products**: the union key set moved by one entry, a remote form of a slug already held, and the **+139** raw `<loc>` entries were a re-shard inside five maps (servers/12 +201, servers/1 -36). Material came from the queue and two feed cards. All five that shipped state a price, a date or a deadline before anything is bought or sent.

- [FaxUp MCP - Send a Fax to 62 Countries From Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/faxup-mcp/) - submission **#7833**, nine keyless tools and the first fax entry here. `send_fax` never sends: it returns a confirmation link. **62** countries; `find_agency_fax_number("IRS")` returns **eight** numbers split by state across two CAF units with the source and a **2026-11-12** check date; a three-page quote is **$2.99** with packs from 5 for $3.99 to 100 for $39.99.
- [Fox Davidson MCP - UK Property Finance Calculators](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/fox-davidson-uk-mortgage-calculators-mcp/) - a feed card. Fifteen keyless UK calculators. Stamp duty at GBP 450,000 returns **12,500** in England and **17,750** in Scotland for a first-time buyer, both reproducible from the returned bands. A buy-to-let stress test reproduces three ways (11,225 at 4.49%, 13,750 at the 5.5% stress rate, ICR 1.50 and 1.22) and names the loan ceiling that passes: **210,658** at 145% ICR. Market rates carry a reviewed date of **2026-11-18**.
- [Daejeon Hankok MCP - A Korean City Priced Per Item](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/daejeon-hankok-mcp/) - submission **#7805**, a reversal of the night pass's scope hold recorded on evidence. **8,627** places and **1,863** stylists over **42** neighbourhoods, plus the Ministry of the Interior's **564** good-value shops with item prices dated **2026-10-18** (찐빵 500원, 아메리카노 1,000원). `get_place` refuses the ids its own search prints, recorded in the guide.
- [CLIA Sentinel MCP - US Lab Certificate Expiry Dates](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/clia-certificate-sentinel-mcp/) - submission **#7835**. A free sample returns a complete CLIA record: expiry **2027-10-19**, **332** days left, the 42 CFR 493.37(f)(1) window open from **2026-10-19** to **2027-01-19** with **59** days to close. It declares its own conflicts and refuses to price the penalties because they are adjusted yearly. The paid tool answers with an **x402** challenge of 0.01 USDC beside a documented three-call-a-day free trial.
- [eSIMX MCP - Travel eSIM Plans Priced in USD](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/esimx-mcp/) - a feed card.
